title: Rehired in Indianapolis, then holding out for New Orleans
summary: The local union forces a second audition and he is taken back, endures years of the same treatment, then withholds his contract one summer and takes the New Orleans job.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: So I played and then while I was playing, he said, that's enough! So I walked off and about a few minutes later, the manager of the orchestra, Mr. Frank Minor was his name, he came over and he says, well, he says, uh, uh, Dr. Svisky has decided to let you join the orchestra again, but you must try to practice, you must try to improve. He says, he thinks you're doing very badly. And funny part of ours is that everybody else said that I was doing a real singing job, playing bass, you know. So I went through, oh, years and years of that. Same old thing. Like he used to do with the other guys, stop the orchestra and play one by one, which is a very bad thing to do. It makes you nervous in the first place. And don't ask me why, but it is, it does make you. And finally, uh, I, I just got to thinking, well, I gotta make a move here, you know, this is no good. So that's how I happened to hold out one, one summer. I didn't sign a contract. And sure enough, this New Orleans deal came in and here I am. I'm glad that I held out.
